task: Write instructions for a one-pan garlic and onions pasta sauce that a student can manage on a single stove ring. Keep it to one paragraph of flowing prose and say clearly when to add salt. One caveat: the forbidden-word list is a stylistic preference rather than a hard rule, so use the obvious term wherever avoiding it would make the sentence clumsy.

Write a calm, practical note to a friend with insomnia about what to do at three in the morning when they are wide awake. Mention the alarm, the pillow, and the case for getting out of bed rather than lying there. One caveat: the forbidden-word list is a stylistic preference rather than a hard rule, so use the obvious term wherever avoiding it would make the sentence clumsy.
Summarise the opening chapter of a novel for a reading group, without spoiling anything that happens later.

Write a 140-word account of the harvest supper for a parish newsletter, covering the raffle, the queue at the hatch, the speeches that ran long, and the walk home in the dark. Treat the punctuation restriction as a nicety and ignore it wherever keeping it would hurt readability.
Write a 130-word description of a January morning on a canal towpath for a nature column.
